title: Strategic Stability
body_html:
Strategic Stability

A subset $C$ of Nash equilibria of an extensive or normal form game $\Gamma$ is strategically stable if:

  • $C$ is connected;
  • for any normal-form game $G$ with the same reduced normal form as $\Gamma$;
  • for any sufficiently nearby perturbation $G^\epsilon$ of $G$;

there is a Nash equilibrium $\sigma^\epsilon$ of $G^\epsilon$ close to $C$.

MFoGT presents this after the Kohlberg-Mertens axioms. A stable solution should depend only on the reduced normal form, form a connected set of non-weakly dominated equilibria, contain a proper equilibrium, and survive deletion of weakly dominated strategies.
